harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured and verified inventory-worker on node1. It runs under OpenRC as the unprivileged inventorysvc account inside a root-owned chroot, with /var/lib/inventory as its only writable application directory. The existing Alpine release and kernel were preserved. A single node reboot confirmed automatic service, mount, confinement, and data recovery.
actions_performed: Created the inventorysvc system account with a nologin shell.
Created a minimal root-owned BusyBox/musl chroot at /var/lib/inventory-chroot.
Created /var/lib/inventory with inventorysvc ownership and mounted it inside the chroot using persistent nodev,nosuid,noexec bind-mount options.
Created and enabled the inventory-worker OpenRC service with no-new-privileges.
Verified OpenRC stop/start behavior and filesystem confinement.
Restarted node1 exactly once and verified its changed boot identity and full recovery.
Removed temporary write-probe artifacts after verification.

evidence.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Alpine Linux v3.23 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts were observed before configuration and remained unchanged after restart.

evidence.requirement: Run the worker as dedicated unprivileged account inventorysvc
evidence.summary: Account uses /sbin/nologin; the live worker runs with UID 103, GID 104, and NoNewPrivs enabled.

evidence.requirement: Manage the background worker as inventory-worker
evidence.summary: OpenRC successfully stopped and started the worker, enables it in the default runlevel, and reports it started after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Confine the filesystem view to a root-owned chroot
evidence.summary: The live process root is /var/lib/inventory-chroot; the jail and runtime tree are root-owned, and host /etc is unavailable inside it.

evidence.requirement: Make /var/lib/inventory the only writable application directory
evidence.summary: Unprivileged probes failed for every other jail directory and succeeded only in /var/lib/inventory, both before and after reboot.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 4764a421-b601-4973-8855-d2ca0619516c; reboot acknowledgement was captured; node returned with boot ID e24b136d-2aaa-44d9-88d5-ef7326d8596e; service, bind mount, account, chroot, state, and advancing heartbeat recovered.
